findings.summary: The reported R-004 sequence is corrected, but the operator guide’s unconditional post-delivery stop claim omits a case that can delay stopping by another check: a new command started since the previous check is still young. The `ProgressRule` class docstring repeats that oversimplification.
evidence: docs/agent-task-runs.md: “the next empty check after delivery stops it.”
scripts/task_run/task_run_progress_rule.py: the `ProgressRule` docstring says a delivered request means “the next empty check stops the lane.”
charness-artifacts/spec/lane-progress-rule.md: a command started since the previous check can defer “the request, or the stop” until completion or the next check.
tests/charness_cli/test_task_run_progress_rule.py: `test_a_command_started_after_the_request_is_not_killed_until_it_is_a_window_old` covers a young command after request delivery.
findings.action: Qualify the guide and class docstring: a young command can defer either request delivery or stopping by one check; otherwise, the next empty check after delivery stops the lane.

counterweight_triage.concern: R-003: readers could take the progress windows as a hard wall-clock bound.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The spec and release notes call windows nominal and explicitly disclaim a hard wall-clock bound; no closed-form bound is needed.

counterweight_triage.concern: R-004: the request and stop sequence after a young command was described one check too early.
counterweight_triage.disposition: The guide now says the request is delivered a check later when the command is young, with stopping after delivery; the separate post-delivery young-command case is captured in R-005.

next_move: Clarify the additional young-command exception in the guide and class docstring, then repeat the bounded review.
non_claims: Reviewed the 17 identity-bound inline files only; did not inspect workspace paths, run tests, or independently verify live runtime behavior.
